subject: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamal Singh <jamal.singh@acmehealth.com>; Priya Raj <priya.raj@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Hi Jamal and Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through Acme Health's requirements. Below is a brief recap of what we discussed, the key pain points, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed or misrepresented.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Data residency: All PHI must remain in the US and be logically separated by tenant.
- Network constraints: Acme will be behind a restrictive firewall with limited outbound IPs; explicit allowlist will be required.
- Air-gap consideration: For some environments, an air-gapped on-prem option may be required for future pilots.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logging are must-haves.
- SLAs/uptime: Expectation is enterprise SLAs for production workloads once contract is in place.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- Private/VPC deployment with customer-controlled subnet and outbound egress allowlist.
- Optional on-prem package for air-gapped deployments; we ship a validated installer plus offline packaging for images.
- KMS integrations and HSM support for encryption-at-rest and key rotation.
- Audit logs and extended retention as part of enterprise package.

Action items and next steps
1) I attached our Private/VPC overview and a networking checklist. Please share these with your network and security teams.
2) Jamal / Priya: can you confirm the rough list of outbound IPs or whether Acme prefers we support egress via a NAT in your VPC?
3) Please send a network diagram or a link to one we can reference (VPC ranges, firewalls, proxy). This will speed the validation.
4) Marissa — can you prep standard SOC2 and compliance artifacts so we have them ready for procurement?
5) Book a follow-up technical session next week to go deeper on the installer and firewall rules. I proposed 3 time slots in the calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-overview.pdf, acme-networking-checklist.xlsx

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jamal Singh <jamal.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Raj <priya.raj@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 17:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Camila — solid recap, appreciate it. A few clarifications from our side:

- We need all PHI to remain in US-east only for now. That rules out multi-region failover unless we have contractual assurances on data residency.
- Egress: our infra team prefers to control egress via a NAT gateway in our VPC. We can provide the NAT IPs once Marissa confirms requirements for allowlisting.
- Air-gap: the air-gapped option is likely for a pilot in a regulated lab. Can you share the offline installer sizing and whether the installer requires outbound validation during setup?
- Compliance: procurement will need SOC2, plus a security questionnaire; I will loop procurement on the thread.

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports FIPS-compliant storage options for the on-prem package?

I reviewed the attached networking checklist and added a few comments inline. Will loop procurement shortly.

Best,
Jamal
Principal Architect, Acme Health
jamal.singh@acmehealth.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamal Singh <jamal.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Raj <priya.raj@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private/VPC discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Jamal — great questions. Quick answers below, and I added a few items for the follow-up tech session.

- Data residency: confirmed — we can pin your deployment to us-east and include contractual language around data residency in the SLAs. Marissa, can you start an initial draft of the residency clause?
- Egress/NAT: supported. We can either operate via allowlist of our outbound IPs or route through your NAT gateway. For the Private offering we commonly recommend using your NAT so you have full control.
- Air-gap installer: the offline installer does not require outbound validation by default. It does require a one-time checksum verification which can be performed offline. Installer sizing: the on-prem package installer and images are about 18GB compressed; minimum host requirements are listed in the attached overview.
- FIPS: Redwood supports FIPS-compliant crypto on request for on-prem packages. We will need to confirm binary builds and any additional validation steps.

Follow-up tech session agenda suggestions
- Review allowlist vs NAT deployment flow and tradeoffs
- Walk through the offline installer and checklist items for air-gapped setup
- Discuss KMS integration options and key rotation flow
- Compliance artifacts and timeline for SOC2 + questionnaire responses

Proposed next steps
1) Please upload or share a network diagram and the list of VPC ranges/NAT details.
2) Marissa, I put procurement and legal on copy if they want to jump in. Can you attach SOC2 and standard security artifacts?
3) Jamal / Priya — pick one of the times in the calendar invite or suggest alternatives.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-overview.pdf, acme-networking-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Camila

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Camila — thanks for the recap and for looping me in. I attached the SOC2 summary and our standard security pack to the Hub link included below. I can also prepare a shorter one-page compliance packet tailored for procurement.
